steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Holmium in ion-adsorption clay
form.label: about 2% of the rare earths in clays

steps.text: The seventeen rare earths always occur together, never alone. The heavy ones, holmium among them, are scarce in the hard-rock ores. Their main source is ion-adsorption clay in southern China and Myanmar, where they cling loosely to weathered granite. It is a trace in bastnäsite and monazite.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: No digging is needed for the clays. A salt solution, usually ammonium sulphate, is pumped into the hillside; it washes the rare earths off the clay and drains out at the bottom, where they are precipitated as a mixed carbonate. The method is cheap and can foul soil and water.
steps.india: 2,900 tonnes of rare-earth oxide in 2025, 0.7% of the world, all from monazite in beach sands worked by IREL.

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.text: The mixed carbonate from the clays is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and filtered. There is no hard mineral to break down, and little of the thorium that comes with monazite. What is left is a mixed rare-earth chloride: all the elements still together.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: This is the hard part. Neighbouring rare earths behave almost identically, so the solution is run through hundreds of solvent-extraction stages, each shifting the balance slightly, until holmium comes out on its own as an oxide. China does about 91% of the world's separation.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Holmium oxide is grown into laser crystals, usually holmium-doped YAG, or reduced to metal for magnet pole pieces.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Holmium lasers cut tissue cleanly with little bleeding and are standard for breaking kidney stones and for prostate surgery. Holmium has the strongest magnetic moment of any element, so it concentrates the field in research magnets.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Very little is recovered from old products: each one holds grams, spread thin and hard to collect. Scrap from the factories that make these materials is the main source.
